paper_summary: Microstructural (SEM, EDS map and line-scan, XRD) study of SL150, SLG and SL300 ceramic hollow microspheres (Envirospheres Ltd.) and of the Al99.5 and AlSi12 matrix syntactic foams made from them by pressure infiltration at ~60 vol% sphere content. The sphere wall consists of densely packed Al2O3 needles (5-10 um long, <0.5 um thick) embedded in a mullite plus amorphous SiO2 matrix, so SiO2-rich zones form at the sphere surface. In Al99.5 matrix foams the molten aluminium reduces this amorphous SiO2 (4Al + 3SiO2 -> 2Al2O3 + 3Si), producing gamma-Al2O3 and a degraded ~6 um interface layer that is expected to lower compressive strength, whereas in AlSi12 matrix foams (and in Al-SL300, infiltrated at the lower 690 C) the reaction is suppressed and the sphere walls stay intact with an interface layer under 3 um.

records.sample_label: Al-SL150 (density/porosity values quoted from ref. [3] Orbulov I., Dobranszky J., Period. Polytech. Mech. Eng. 52(1) 2008, 35-42)

processing.particle_grade: SL150 ceramic hollow microspheres (Envirospheres Ltd., Australia); 30-35 wt% Al2O3, 45-50 wt% amorphous SiO2, 19 wt% mullite, 1 wt% quartz, balance other oxides

structure.microstructure_notes: Microsphere size distribution 56-183 um (95% range), specific surface 0.060 1/um. Sphere wall is Al2O3 needles (5-10 um long, <0.5 um diameter) embedded in a mixture of mullite and amorphous SiO2 (SEM/EDS maps). XRD phase content of the foam: Al 67, Si 8, mullite 11, alpha-Al2O3 3, gamma-Al2O3 11, quartz 0, amorphous 0 (wt%). Molten Al reduced the amorphous SiO2-rich zones (4Al + 3SiO2 -> 2Al2O3 + 3Si), producing gamma-Al2O3 and severely degrading the microsphere wall; EDS line scan shows a wide (~6 um) diffuse interface layer with poorly defined outer sphere edge. Particle porosity 50.9%, total porosity 44.7% (Tab. 2).

test.specimen_notes: No mechanical testing in this paper. Characterisation only: density/porosity (Tab. 2, quoted from ref. [3]), XRD phase analysis (Philips X-Pert, CuKalpha, 40 kV / 35 mA, 0.04 deg/s), SEM + EDS maps and 30-point EDS line scans across the sphere/matrix interface (Philips XL-30 with EDAX Genesis, 15 kV) on polished sections.

extraction_notes: This paper reports NO mechanical property measurements (no modulus, strength, energy absorption or hardness numbers), so all Properties fields are null; test.test_type is 'other' because only density/porosity, XRD, SEM and EDS characterisation were performed. data_origin is 'secondary' for all six records because Tab. 2 (theoretical and measured density, particle/matrix/total porosity) is explicitly labelled as taken from ref. [3] (Orbulov I., Dobranszky J., 'Producing metal matrix syntactic foams by pressure infiltration', Period. Polytech. Mech. Eng. 52(1), 2008, 35-42), which is cited in sample_label. The XRD phase data of Tab. 3 and the SEM/EDS observations are primary to this paper and are captured in microstructure_notes. Porosities converted from percent to fractions. matrix_porosity_fraction is NEGATIVE for the three Al99.5 foams (-0.062, -0.058, -0.072); the authors state a negative value means the microspheres themselves were partly infiltrated, so the calculated particle porosity is overestimated - it is not a physical negative porosity. Particle porosity (50.9/49.5/48.2%) and total porosity (44.7-52.0%) have no schema field and are recorded in microstructure_notes. particle_volume_fraction=0.60 from the stated '~60 vol%' and applies to all six foams. Infiltration temperature is given only for Al-SL300 (690 C, stated as the lower temperature that suppressed the reaction); it is null for the other foams. Sphere chemical composition in Tab. 1 is printed once and applies to all three SL grades. Test temperature set to 25 C as a default for room-temperature characterisation.
